lines: An AI agent can hold money, but it can't open an AWS account.
And if you own an idle server, there's no simple way to let a stranger use it for ten minutes.
Sublet fixes both.
It rents out any Linux machine by the minute, with nothing installed on it.
Here's how it works.
The owner lists their machine on a NEAR smart contract.
NEAR's MPC network derives a signing key that only this contract can use.
The owner adds that key to their server with one line of SSH config.
That's the whole setup.
Now a tenant, a person or an AI agent, wants the machine, so they pay the rent.
The contract checks the price.
Then it writes an SSH certificate from the owner's public terms: who can log in, for how long, and what they can run.
The MPC network signs those exact bytes.
No single node ever holds the key.
The tenant logs in with ordinary SSH.
The server checks the signature by itself.
It never talks to a blockchain.
Tenants can also pay in USDC on Base, straight to the owner.
The contract never touches that money.
It asks the MPC network to read the payment from Base, with no bridge, and then cuts the key the same way.
Here's a real lease on a stock Debian server.
With no lease, the door is shut.
Rent it, and SSH works.
OpenSSH only checks a certificate at login, so the contract signs a timer into it.
When the time runs out, the session is killed, and the same key is refused.
The contract has zero access keys, so nobody can change its code.
We ran thirty-seven attacks against it, and all of them were stopped.
AI agents get the same tools through an MCP server.
It's unaudited and on testnet, and you can re-check the evidence yourself with one command.
This is Sublet, built at NEAR Hackathon.
